2608.10949.title: StreamFlow: Dynamic Memory Flows for Streaming Video Understanding
2608.10949.paper_summary: Streaming video understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to preserve relevant evidence from continuously evolving streams under strict causality and bounded memory. Yet existing paradigms remain limited: model-based methods require intrusive backbone updates, while memory-based methods expend substantial visual-encoding computation on temporally redundant content and rely on rigid access to visual history. To address these limitations, we introduce StreamFlow, an efficient visual memory framework that enables dynamic, on-demand access to historical visual information. StreamFlow combines a lightweight, dynamics-aware mid-term memory that filters temporal redundancy before visual encoding with a latent long-term memory that consolidates historical video content into visual latents accessible to subsequent reasoning. During generation, an attention-guided retrieval mechanism injects relevant visual latents when the model's reliance on visual evidence weakens. StreamFlow achieves state-of-the-art streaming video understanding performance, reaching 67.73% overall accuracy on StreamingBench, while also delivering strong performance on offline long-video benchmarks. Relative to the vanilla setting, it improves the visual attention score (VAS) by 59.1% while reducing end-to-end latency and peak memory by 50.4% and 21.1%, respectively, enabling more visually grounded and efficient reasoning.
2608.10949.paper_summary_zh: 串流視頻理解需要多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）在嚴格的因果關係和有限的記憶下，保存來自不斷演變的串流中的相關證據。<lb/>然而，現有的範式仍然有限：基於模型的方法需要侵入性的骨幹更新，而基於記憶的方法在時間上冗餘的內容上消耗大量的視覺編碼計算，並依賴於對視覺歷史的僵化訪問。<lb/>為了解決這些限制，我們介紹了StreamFlow，一個高效的視覺記憶框架，能夠動態地按需訪問歷史視覺信息。<lb/>StreamFlow結合了一個輕量級、動態感知的中期記憶，該記憶在視覺編碼之前過濾時間冗餘，以及一個潛在的長期記憶，將歷史視頻內容整合成可供後續推理訪問的視覺潛在。<lb/>在生成過程中，當模型對視覺證據的依賴減弱時，一個注意力引導的檢索機制會注入相關的視覺潛在。<lb/>StreamFlow實現了最先進的串流視頻理解性能，在StreamingBench上達到67.73%的整體準確率，同時在離線長視頻基準測試中也表現出色。<lb/>相較於原始設置，它將視覺注意力得分（VAS）提高了59.1%，同時將端到端延遲和峰值記憶分別減少了50.4%和21.1%，從而實現了更具視覺基礎和高效的推理。
